items.title: SPHMC Wasserstein-to-phase-state second moment

source.anchor: Lemma D.4 proof, PDF page 56; equation (D.3) and Lemma 4.16
source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. Samplinglib expands the standard coupling/integrability step; this is not the authors' wording or a complete Lemma D.4 claim.

items.statement: A quadratic Wasserstein estimate transfers reference phase-coordinate second moments to the incoming law; the current compiled adapter uses the ordinary product metric and keeps the paper's M_kappa comparison open.
assumptions: Lipschitz observable with an integrable reference second moment.
Finite ordinary squared Wasserstein radius stated using Samplinglib's ENNReal W2.
For the phase adapter, separate reference position and momentum moments.

obligations.label: W2 transfer for Lipschitz observable second moments
M_kappa metric definition and norm comparison (remaining)
All actual Picard query-center gradient moments (remaining)

bindings.boundary: Ordinary quadratic W2 and one observable only; no optimal coupling, twisted metric or SPHMC history.

assumption_deltas.source: Lemma D.4 uses Wasserstein control to infer second moments without isolating a theorem.
assumption_deltas.lean: The observable is explicitly b-Lipschitz and square-integrable under the reference measure; integrability under the transported measure is a conclusion.
assumption_deltas.reason: Real integral inequalities require the involved moments to be integrable.

assumption_deltas.source: The paper can appeal to optimal couplings in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
assumption_deltas.lean: The proof uses arbitrarily near-optimal couplings and therefore does not assume attainment.
assumption_deltas.reason: This weakens the proof infrastructure without changing the bound.

bindings.boundary: Ordinary product max metric only. No M_kappa comparison, (D.3), run history, complete D.7, D.8 or main theorem.

assumption_deltas.source: The paper controls W_{2,M_kappa} and invokes uniform equivalence with Euclidean phase energy.
assumption_deltas.lean: The current theorem assumes Samplinglib's ordinary product-metric W2 bound.
assumption_deltas.reason: Lean's product norm is max norm; the explicit M_kappa linear metric and comparison constants are the next separate theorem.

assumption_deltas.source: The stationary phase law and Lemma 4.16 supply its moments in the paper.
assumption_deltas.lean: Reference position/momentum integrability and bounds Mx,Mp are explicit premises.
assumption_deltas.reason: Constructing the smoothed stationary phase law and proving its moments remain independent inputs.
